subject: Post-call: StreamlinePay latency/throughput commitment & next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa@streamlinepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — latency & throughput needs, recommended path

Thanks for taking the time earlier today, Alyssa — quick written recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture. I left the call with three signals that will drive the recommended deployment mode:

1) Latency target (p95): 30 ms at checkout (non-negotiable per Alyssa)
2) Peak throughput: ~400 concurrent requests during promo bursts, sustained baseline ~50 qps
3) Data handling: card tokenization is done upstream, but you require a dedicated VPC for PCI controls + audit logs

Initial recommendation (high level):
- Dedicated (reserved) capacity for production: Given the 30 ms p95 requirement and the sustained/peak QPS profile, a Dedicated pool with reserved GPU capacity plus NVMe-backed KV cache looks like the most realistic path to hit targets consistently.
- Hosted API for early-stage experimentation: We can run a short hosted pilot to validate prompt engineering and correctness but do not recommend relying on hosted for the checkout lane at scale.
- Private VPC: required for your compliance posture; we should scope whether Private (VPC) can be combined with Dedicated for the pilot or whether separate on-prem considerations are needed.

Ask list / next steps:
- StreamlinePay: share 72-hour traffic trace (timestamped qps, concurrent counts) and a representative sample of request payloads (PII redacted) — Alyssa, can you confirm by EOD Wed?
- Redwood: run a focused 1-hour benchmark (we will emulate 30 ms p95 target and the 400 concurrent burst) and share a short report + preliminary sizing and costs. We’ll attach the benchmark-summary and estimate.
- Legal/Procurement: Ben, I’ll loop you in after we confirm sizing so you can start a draft SOW and an outline of reserved capacity terms.

Tentative timeline: preliminary benchmark and cost ballpark by Thu 5/30, SOW draft the following week, pilot kickoff the week of 6/10 if all aligns.

Attachments: benchmark-summary-2028-05-28.txt (prelim), pilot_sow-draft-v1.pdf (placeholder), streamlinepay_qps_profile.csv (template).

Hannah Schmitt
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
(hannah.schmitt@redwood.com)

--
On Tue, 28 May 2028 at 15:45, Alyssa Park <alyssa@streamlinepay.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Hannah — appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick notes:
> - The 30 ms p95 requirement is for all checkout-facing inference calls (session scoring + fraud filter enrichment). It is business critical.
> - Peak 400 concurrent is correct for marketing bursts; baseline 40–60 qps depending on region.
> - We need a solution that supports a dedicated VPC and audit logs; we already have a KMS in GCP.
>
> Alyssa
> Director, Engineering — StreamlinePay
From: Alyssa Park <alyssa@streamlinepay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — latency & throughput needs, recommended path

Hannah — quick reply while I’m out of meetings.

Confirmation: the 30 ms p95 is non-negotiable for checkout. If that forces Dedicated + VPC, we accept that, but we need a ballpark on cost and an example pilot cadence (how long to validate, what we need to provide). Also: any caching recommendations (prefix vs full KV) that reduce the GPU footprint are useful — our infra team would prefer fewer GPUs if we can meet latency via caching.

I can share the 72-hour trace by tomorrow EOD; I’ll redact PII and send. Also include any sample request size limits you need.

Thanks — Alyssa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Park <alyssa@streamlinepay.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap — latency & throughput needs, recommended path

Looping in a technical viewpoint and quick cost posture. Key points from infra/readout: 

- Hit 30 ms p95 target: realistic with Dedicated if we apply the following combo — small-batch decoding (micro-batching tuned to 2–4 requests), aggressive KV prefix caching for the common session payloads, and a quantized model path for the checkout-critical route. That narrows GPU selection to A100/RTX-class with NVMe cache.
- Sizing: initial pilot we recommend reserving 4 GPUs (to emulate burst handling with controlled load), production reserved pool estimate: 8 GPUs with autoscale headroom for promo bursts.
- Timeline: We can run a 1-hour stress benchmark within 48 hours of receiving the traffic trace + sample payloads. Report includes p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, and cache hit ratio.
- Ballpark cost (pre-negotiation): pilot (4 GPUs, 2 weeks) ~ $18k–24k; production reserved (8 GPUs) monthly ~$68k–$95k depending on duration of commit and cache sizing. I’ll put a clean estimate in the shared Drive.

Attachments: benchmark-summary-2028-05-28.txt (prelim). Action: Hannah — can you confirm we ask StreamlinePay for sample payloads limited to 1 MB compressed per request and the 72-hour trace in CSV? I’ll prepare an amended SOW and a procurement checklist.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa@streamlinepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — latency & throughput needs, recommended path — next steps

Perfect — thanks for the quick confirmations, Alyssa and Ben. Summarizing agreed next steps and owners so nothing falls through: 

1) StreamlinePay (Alyssa) — share 72-hour traffic trace (CSV) + 10 representative, redacted request payloads (<=1 MB compressed) by EOD Thu 5/30.
2) Redwood (Ben & SE team) — run 1-hour focused benchmark against a dedicated pool emulating the 400-concurrent burst; deliver p50/p95/p99 and cache hit metrics by Fri 5/31. Ben to prepare pilot estimate and updated SOW.
3) Redwood Legal/Procurement — Ben to circulate pilot SOW draft (pilot scope, reserved capacity terms, data access controls) by Tue 6/4.
4) Ops/Infra alignment — Sean will scope VPC/KMS onboarding steps and share a checklist for firewall rules and peering.

Can we tentatively pencil the pilot kickoff window 6/10–6/14? If the benchmark is green and StreamlinePay signs the pilot SOW, that timeline is achievable. I’ll create a short tracking doc in Drive and share the link.

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with the Drive link and the benchmark report once Ben’s run completes.

Hannah Schmitt
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
(hannah.schmitt@redwood.com)

Attachments referenced: pilot_sow-draft-v1.pdf, benchmark-summary-2028-05-28.txt
